reason: Schedule and feasibility lens: the idea SURVIVES, with two build repairs. A scored probe fits easily before 29 Sep 10:00 UTC. It needs no training, no new weights and no Kaggle dataset: the x138 datasets stay as they are, and the only code change is a patch in cell 4. P(scored in time) is about 0.8 (a guess). Components: build and CPU-mock test pass within 2 attempts ~0.9; dummy run passes ~0.95; the user OKs one of the 20 slots on 26-29 Sep ~0.95. The critical path has ~60 h of slack, enough for two rebuild cycles. Checked facts: (1) Frame t is detected only from its first window. The seen_frames gate is at tools/repo/scripts/predict_unet_transformer.py l.394-404, and the detection loss averages all W frames (train_unet_transformer.py l.842-849). Both are confirmed. (2) I replayed x138 cell-4 patches (cell lines 10-310 and 481-533) on a scratch copy of tools/repo's predict script. Every predict_video anchor matched: 8-view TTA, dual-seed 1-4, retention guard, bidirectional, manifest, ILP timeout, edge-TTA, secondary TTA, lowdet dump and V1284 (a)-(c). Only 2 main()-level anchors differ from the Kaggle support-pack version, so the patched loop can be rebuilt here for a CPU mock test. (3) In the patched script the detection block (l.625-642) holds lowdet plus _v1284_refine. The edge loop (l.649-893) reads only unet_out, secondary_unet_out, frame_indices and coords_so_far, plus the closures all_edges and seen_pairs, and it sits at 8-space indent. It can be lifted verbatim into a nested def and called one window later with the previous window's cached tensors. The 'delay refactor' is therefore a moderate string patch (about 3-5 agent-hours incl. tests), not a rewrite. (4) encode() = unet(window), then a per-frame detect_head. TemporalUNet3D's temporal attention is plain MHA with NO time position embedding (temporal_unet.py l.30-50, l.125-129), so for W=2 the net is equivariant under time permutation. The pos-0 and pos-1 logits are the same function of (self, neighbour), which removes the idea's calibration risk (2). (5) Runtime: the x138 dummy run takes ~40 min on T4 (experiments/RESULTS.md, exp56 row). tempfuse adds no encode, only one map mean and one top-K per frame. Cached features are ~67 MB per model (2x32x64^3 fp32), so the 12 h limit and GPU memory are not at risk. What fails AS WRITTEN: (a) The per-VIDEO quantile-match guard cannot be implemented in the streaming single pass. It needs every frame's fused map before any detection, while edges must run one window later. Caching every window's features costs ~67 MB x 2 models x ~100 windows ≈ 13 GB per shard with 2 shards, and re-encoding doubles GPU time, which breaks 'zero extra GPU'. (b) 'Byte-identical with TEMPFUSE=0' can only hold at the output level (coords and edges), not for the notebook, since the patch text is added. (c) The 'agent-container' resource cannot push or run kernels. kaggle.com returns 403 through this proxy (verified by the sibling v_github-intel_successor-port_schedule.json), so pushes go through the laptop agent that holds kaggle.json (CONTEXT.md l.39). The user's offer to paste the Kaggle API key into this chat would not help (the domain is blocked here), and a secret should not be pasted into chat. (d) tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 accepts only divinsert and leafprune (l.12-16), so a BASES/patch whitelist entry is needed (~0.5 h). None of these blocks the schedule. Caveat outside my lens (for the value reviewer): the adoption gate is base + 0.002, LB noise is ~0.003 and the central expected gain is +0.001. One probe will most likely return 'tie', so the slot buys little information. It is best spent as the planned F2 node-set diversifier or stacked on a probe that is already running.
fix_if_any: (1) Replace the per-video quantile guard with a PER-FRAME top-K guard, computed at fusion time. Set K = the number of pos-1 peaks >= 0.965 on the pos-1 map for that frame. Take the local maxima (_detect_cells_pooled at a low threshold, e.g. 0.3, which the lowdet dump already computes) of the fused map and keep the top K by fused value. Clamp so |K_fused - K| <= max(1, 1%). Dump lowdet peaks from the FUSED map, rescaling scores so the per-frame cutoff maps to 0.965; readmit (MIN_SCORE 0.965) then stays consistent. (2) Implement the delay by lifting the edge block (patched l.649-893) into a nested def _tf_edges(unet_out, secondary_unet_out, frame_indices, coords_so_far). Per window: fuse and register frame ws (cached pos-1 logits plus current pos-0 logits; V1284 refine uses the CACHED pos-1 features, as today). Hold frame ws+1's final det map and features. Run _tf_edges on the previous window's cache. After the loop, register the last frame from one view and flush the last window's edges. Global ids stay in frame order. Assert every anchor exactly once, as x138 does. Add the patch to build_probe_kernel.py for --base x138 (and exp39 as a fallback if #34 < 0.953). (3) Before any GPU: pip install CPU torch + tracksdata + zarr here. Replay the x138 cell-4 patches onto tools/repo's script (skip the 2 main() anchors). Run predict_video on a synthetic 4-6 frame zarr with a same-architecture local checkpoint (weights_dataset/exp03B) and V1284_MODE=zero. Assert that TEMPFUSE=0 coords and edges equal unpatched exactly; that TEMPFUSE=1 has identical seen_pairs coverage and per-frame counts within the clamp; and that the peak-set change is in the 1-10% band. (4) The dummy-run log must print per-frame peak IoU (pos-1 vs fused), node counts and pair coverage. (5) Use max-fusion as the backup knob (TEMPFUSE=2) in the same build, not a second build.
realistic_public_gain: +0.000 to +0.002 (central +0.001, a guess). Below the +0.002 gate and inside the ~0.003 LB noise, so a single probe most likely reads as a tie.
realistic_private_gain: +0.000 to +0.002 (guess). A model-side 2-view ensemble with the node count held per frame should transfer about as well as it does on public.
